clue.text: Threaten with very angry corgis, initially backing warning to postman?

indicators.note: backing means running in reverse, so the whole string built from the preceding pieces is read from its end

parts.note: to threaten is to menace

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A postman is warned off by a sign about very fierce corgis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the whole run MENACEVAC round. CAVE CANEM is Latin for 'beware of the dog', the classic sign by a front gate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means beware of the dog, a notice aimed at callers like the person delivering letters.

clue.text: Return special papers, being apathetic

indicators.note: return means send back, so the word for special is written backwards

parts.note: a pet project or pet subject is a special favourite one
ID, identity documents, are papers

explanation.surface: Someone sends back their special documents, showing no enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' applies only to the word for special; the papers follow in normal order.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm in feeling, so showing little interest or enthusiasm, is the figurative sense of the word.

clue.text: Alloy also used for bottle

definitions.meaning: a yellow metal made of copper and zinc
British slang for courage or nerve, as is its partner word, slang for cheek

explanation.surface: A metal is used to make a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' looks like a container; in British slang it means nerve, and so does brass (cheek, effrontery).
explanation.definitionFit: Copper-zinc metal on one side, and British slang for nerve or impudence on the other.

clue.text: When route diverted, it's to which place?

indicators.note: a diverted route is sent another way, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver on a diverted road wonders where it now leads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' rearranges the nine letters of WHEN ROUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned interrogative adverb meaning towards what place or to what end.

clue.text: New side to build upright?

indicators.note: to build is to put together, so the letters of the two words are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for adding a new wing to a building, set upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to build' rearranges NEW SIDE; 'New' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: With the end foremost or standing on end, so vertical rather than lying flat.

clue.text: One raising a glass, something brown or white in it?

definitions.meaning: a person proposing a toast at a dinner

definitions.text: something brown or white in it?
definitions.meaning: a kitchen appliance that holds slices of brown or white bread

explanation.surface: A diner raises a glass, holding a brown or white drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brown or white' suggests ale or wine in the glass; it is bread in the kitchen gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a person who proposes a health and an appliance for browning slices of bread.

clue.text: All in order so — these words?

definitions.text: All in order so — these words?

parts.words: All in order so — these words
parts.note: the initial letters A, I, O, S, T, W of the six words run in the sequence of the ABC, so the clue words themselves illustrate the way they are arranged

explanation.surface: Someone checks that everything is tidy and asks about these words.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue demonstrates itself: All, in, order, so, these, words begin with letters in ABC sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged by the sequence of the letters from A to Z, as the clue words are.

clue.text: Woman's 'holiday' relative, yet man in a tizzy

indicators.note: a tizzy is a state of nervous agitation, so the letters of the three words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A man gets flustered while a female relative takes time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a tizzy' rearranges RELATIVE YET MAN; 'holiday' is in quotes because time off to have a baby is hardly a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Time away from work granted to a mother around the birth of her child, jokingly called a break.

clue.text: Act of entering second behind artist

indicators.note: behind says the letter for second comes after the painter's name

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French painter

explanation.surface: A second visitor enters behind a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal word for going in, or the right of entry, as opposed to egress.

clue.text: Cloth stuffed in mouth in desperate need to be tied up

indicators.note: in places the piece of cloth inside the rearranged letters
desperate suggests wild disorder, so the letters of the word need are rearranged

parts.note: a gag is a cloth pushed into the mouth to silence someone

explanation.surface: A kidnap scene: a gagged captive desperately needing to be bound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate need' reads as one phrase, but 'desperate' is the anagram signal; 'tied up' means busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy or occupied, as a telephone line or a person with commitments is, so not free.

clue.text: As Napoleon might have said: 'Good Lord, strange one's beaten!'

parts.note: a French speaker like Napoleon would say bon for good
the Lord is God
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Napoleon exclaims in surprise at a strange defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word for good is followed by GOD and RUM; 'beaten' suggests military defeat, but the answer is an instrument struck by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hand drum, something played by being struck or beaten.

clue.text: Dribble in game, turning on defender's outside

indicators.note: outside picks the outer letters of the word defender's, its first and last
turning means the card game's name is read backwards

parts.note: loo is an old card game

explanation.surface: A footballer dribbles past a defender, turning on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' gives D and R from defender's; 'turning' makes LOO into OOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To let saliva run from the mouth, which is one sense of dribbling.

clue.text: Herb in porridge, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for porridge is said out loud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: British slang for a jail sentence, i.e. time served in prison

explanation.surface: Someone detects a herb in their breakfast oats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porridge' is British slang for doing time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant culinary plant of the mint family used in cooking.

clue.text: Indian language that can be read as Arabic?

indicators.text: that can be read as Arabic?
indicators.note: Arabic script runs right to left, so a word that reads the same in that direction as in English is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An Indian language that might be mistaken for Arabic.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome: read right to left, as Arabic is, it is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dravidian language spoken mainly in the southern Indian state of Kerala.

clue.text: Case of chauffeur maintaining fit roughly in vehicle

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the outer pair encloses the other pieces
the case of a word is its outside, here its first and last letters

parts.note: fit and able both mean capable
CA, circa, means approximately

explanation.surface: A chauffeur keeps fit, roughly speaking, in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of' gives C and R from chauffeur, which hold ABLE and CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A carriage hauled on a wire rope, a kind of transport.

clue.text: Various inedible starters accompanying a tasty dish

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: accompanying means along with, and

explanation.surface: Diners are served inedible starters with a tasty main dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' suggests a meal's first courses but takes V and I.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or literary word for an item of food, especially a delicacy.

clue.text: Discipline players, one and all at the game

parts.note: the cast are the actors in a play
I is the Roman numeral one
the gate is the total attendance at a sports match

explanation.surface: A coach disciplines all the players at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke or punish severely, to chastise.

clue.text: Unplaced, having just pulled up?

definitions.meaning: in a race, finishing outside the first few places
a car that has just stopped is present at this moment, split as two words meaning at present and in this place

explanation.surface: A racehorse finishes unplaced after pulling up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' suggests a horse stopping in a race; read as a car arriving it means present at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing slang: a horse that is out of the placings finishes nowhere.

clue.text: Short hallucinogenic experience inferior to same high for wizards

indicators.note: inferior to means below, so in a down clue the shortened word goes under the jumbled letters
high means drugged up, so the letters of same are scrambled
short means cut off, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a trip is a session under a drug such as LSD

explanation.surface: A drug trip leaves someone feeling high, as if surrounded by wizards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' scrambles same; 'Short' clips the trip, and 'inferior to' places it below in this down clue. Wizards here are experts, not magicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of an Italian word for masters of an art, especially great conductors; wizards in the sense of experts.

clue.text: Eighth in alphabet: eighth letter: a Greek character!

definitions.text: Eighth in alphabet: eighth letter: a Greek character!

indicators.note: eighth in picks the letter in eighth position of the word alphabet

parts.note: H is the eighth letter of the English alphabet
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A quiz fact about the eighth letter of the alphabet and a Greek character.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the answer is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter in eighth position, between eta and iota.

clue.text: Smoke pot with a cashier, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks for the phrase to be spoken out loud to give a differently spelt word

parts.note: pot is pan, a stays as written, and a cashier is a teller

explanation.surface: Someone shares cannabis with a bank cashier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoke' and 'pot' suggest cannabis; the smoke is a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin cigar, something one smokes.

clue.text: Fish gulping oxygen beginning to breathe — I forget what that's called

indicators.note: gulping means swallowing, so the fish takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a dory is a sea fish, the John Dory
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A fish gulps oxygen as it starts to breathe, and its name escapes the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: O and B go inside DORY.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a thingummy, a word used for an object whose name one cannot recall.

clue.text: Resonating quality in design, roofless office

parts.note: a design is a plan

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: an agency is a business office

explanation.surface: Resonance is part of the design of an office with no roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roofless' drops the top letter of AGENCY in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, often melancholy, ringing or resonant tone; the abstract noun for a resonant sound.

clue.text: Supposedly old story, not new, penned by friend

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed, so the shortened story goes inside the friend

parts.note: an ally is a friend

indicators.note: not new says the abbreviation for new is removed

parts.note: a legend is a traditional old story

explanation.surface: An old story, supposedly, written by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not new' drops N from the old story before 'penned by' puts it inside the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportedly or as claimed, without proof: an adverb meaning according to what is said.

clue.text: Prize involving death with leader in uprising — one swings?

indicators.note: involving means including, so the prize holds the other letters

parts.note: a plum job is a prize one
end means death

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone wins a prize after a leader dies in an uprising, and one swings for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' looks like a reversal signal in this down clue but simply gives its first letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight hung from a fixed point that swings to and fro, as in a clock.

clue.text: No problem stealing heart of matron to get medicine?

indicators.note: stealing means taking in, so the sum encloses the middle letters

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, here the two central letters

explanation.surface: A matron's heart is stolen: no problem, a dose of medicine will cure it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes the two central letters of an even-length word; a nostrum is a dubious cure, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack remedy, a medicine of doubtful worth; the question mark admits it may not be real medicine.

clue.text: Current article requires qualification, separating Right and Left

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: separating means coming between, so the degree sits inside the two direction letters

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is an academic qualification

explanation.surface: A politics article requires qualification to separate right from left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present, but is a noun: a rising air current.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising current of warm air, as used by gliders and birds.

clue.text: Giant lifted onto stake as means of execution

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means turned upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: giant means big
a stake is a bet, a sum wagered

explanation.surface: A giant is hoisted on a stake for execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' reverses BIG to GIB in this down clue; 'stake' suggests burning but means a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallows-like post from which executed bodies were hung.

clue.text: Escape together, as damsel opens traps

indicators.note: traps means catches inside, so the answer is held in the words damsel opens

explanation.surface: A damsel opens traps to escape with her lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traps' holds the answer across damsEL OPEns.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away secretly to marry, as two lovers do.

clue.text: Develop lungs, primarily, for roar?

parts.note: to develop is to grow

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the first letter of lungs is taken

explanation.surface: Someone develops their lungs, mainly in order to roar.
explanation.definitionFit: A low, rumbling or angry roar, as from a dog or bear.
